entries.name: miso_rdt_tcdc (RDT 92% default derate + $40/$500 TCDC tiers)
entries.where: constants.MISO_RDT_* via transmission.apply_miso_rdt_tcdc; priced one-way tiers (TransferLink.flow_cost)
entries.source: 2024 MISO SOM §III.B (92% default derate; two-step TCDC $40 at the modeled limit, $500 from 102%); MISO/SPP JOA Attach. A (3,000 N->S / 2,500 S->N contract limits)
entries.note: deliberately conservative: the 92% DEFAULT derate is used, not the deeper condition-driven operator derates (utilization averaged 84% of contract when binding in 2024, SOM §II.E) — no published hourly derate series, so binding-hour congestion under-shoots rather than fitting a haircut; re-derives only when MISO publishes new TCDC/derate parameters (rule 23)

entries.name: miso_rpe_pricing (RPE $200 additive on RDT violation tiers)
entries.where: constants.MISO_RPE_DEMAND_VALUE via transmission.apply_miso_rdt_tcdc (rpe_pricing=True); adds to the two violation tiers' TransferLink.flow_cost only
entries.source: 2024 MISO SOM §II.E ('MISO enforces STR requirements in its two subregions by enforcing reserve procurement enhancement (RPE) constraints over the RDT') + §III.B (single $200/MWh demand value; RDT+RPE 'apply additively' in real violations — measured $700 spreads, small violations overpriced by $200); IMM Summer-2025 quarterly ($41M RDT+RPE congestion, +121% YoY)
entries.note: deliberately conservative: the RPE's STR-scarcity binding channel (binds with NO RDT violation when importing-subregion STR is limited — the quarterly's 'RPE Only' category) is unrepresented because the LP carries no STR product, so separation under-shoots; the IMM's cap-at-$500 recommendation was not implemented in-window — date-gate the re-anchor if MISO adopts it (rule 23)

entries.name: unit_outage_short_windows (< 5-day baseload-coal CEMS windows)

entries.source: per-unit EPA CAMPD hourly gross generation (scripts/derive_campd_unit_outages.py --short-windows); identification guards: coal-only detector + unit annual CF >= 0.55 (the partial-outage detector's baseload constant) + the revealed-availability in-merit filter (derive_campd_outages.filter_revealed_outages; the full-stop override cannot engage below the 5-day cap)
entries.note: the >= 5-day duration floor makes event-coincident short forced outages invisible (MISO Jul 28-29 2025: ~2.8 GW coal offline at the peak block beyond the overlay; docs/DIAGNOSIS-miso-july2025-lmp-2026-07.md); CT/CC event unavailability stays unmodeled pending a max-gen-event registry intake (no identification without it)

entries.name: carry_operating_mothballs (OA-but-operating re-carry, vintage-status oracle)

entries.source: EIA-860 year-matched vintage status (vintage_<Y>/eia860_generators.parquet): a unit OA in the 2025ER canonical snapshot is re-carried for solve year Y iff OP in vintage_<Y> (Cottonwood 55358: 4 of 8 units OA, ~572.6 MW vintage_2023 / ~568.7 MW vintage_2024, with CAMPD showing the OA CTs running 88-91% of 2023 hours). Real units at availability bounds — never a CAMPD-MWh pin or a MW offset (rules 1/11/13). Design: docs/handoffs/miso-cc-vintage-undercarry-plan-2026-07.md
entries.note: regenerates for any forward vintage (a unit OP in its latest vintage is physically available until a real exit removes it — rule 12 forward story); the LP dispatches the carried units freely (no outcome pinning)

entries.name: MISO COAL SOM near-cost offer floor
entries.where: pipeline/backcast_config.py _MISO_OFFER_CURVE COAL_* entries (committed/econ_low = 1.00) + calibration_flags coal_prb/bit_passthrough_sigmoid=False, coal_prb_passthrough_tiered=False
entries.source: the MISO IMM's measured conduct statistics (datatype som-competitive-conduct; freeze test tests/test_curate_som_competitive_conduct.py): system price-cost mark-up +3.0% (2023) / -2.5% (2024) — offers AT reference levels ~= SRMC — and output gap 'effectively de minimis' (0.1%/0.06% of load; 2025 quarterlies 22-71 MW/hr). The measured discount depth is ~none, so every MISO coal tranche above must-run bids full measured F923 delivered SRMC: the gas-keyed passthrough sigmoid MECHANISM is replaced for MISO (not re-parameterized) and the sub-1.0 band multipliers raised to exactly 1.00 — a zero-discount anchor, no fitted value (n_scalars 0). Self-commitment (SOM Table 7: must-run status on 56%/53% of regulated coal starts) remains represented by the per-plant fuel-free _mustrun band (coal_mustrun_per_plant, CAMPD thermal_tranches_MISO.csv), one mechanism per phenomenon (rule 19). Adjudication record: docs/handoffs/miso-coal-offer-som-redesign-2026-07.md. Re-derive trigger: the 2025 MISO SOM publication (rule 23).

entries.name: gas_daily_shape[MISO]
entries.where: backcast_config.py gas_daily_shape (MISO added 2026-07-09); factors from data/raw/gas-prices/henry_hub_daily.csv via fuel.gas_daily_shape_factors
entries.source: measured Henry Hub daily spot (EIA RNGWHHD), normalized to each month's own daily mean (mean-preserving, so the monthly EIA-923 plant-level delivered gas level and the annual mix are unchanged); no fitted value — the factors ARE the data. Forward-reproducible (a forward monthly level times a representative daily shape). Closes the miso-50 rule-23 granularity caveat's free-data leg; the daily basin-basis leg (Chicago Citygate daily) remains the open paywalled ask.

entries.name: hydro 2025 completeness (backfill 2024 + EIA-930 monthly repin)
entries.where: run_config.calibration_flags hydro_backfill_year=2024, hydro_eia930_monthly=true (the PJM/NEISO keeper pattern)

Backcast-only measured input (rule 13-admissible: physical inflow availability); the forecast path uses the normal-water-year climatology instead.
